Independent reduced-neck canonicalization also reproduces the read-across coincidence counts 932/1000 and 5415/5832 and the named stable, drifting and splitting slots. The finite tables are internally correct under the stated multiplication convention.

originality.rationale: Neretin’s 2025 paper defines these exact relative class algebras and gives a general structure-constant formula for arbitrary Young subgroups. The displayed S4/S5/S6 tables are direct finite specializations of that formula and of the class-sum definition. The read-across counts are obtained mechanically by comparing those directly computed specializations. A search found no identical printed table, but implication-based originality treats such special cases of a stronger general result as covered.

value.rationale: The relative stabilization problem is mathematically motivated, but this record establishes no stabilization theorem, obstruction, threshold or structural lemma. It reports small multiplication tables and slot-by-slot coincidence percentages generated by routine finite enumeration from an existing general formula. Those data are reproducible, yet as a standalone finding they do not clear the bar against known-formula recomputation and arbitrary small-instance tabulation.

scientific_limitations: No evidence was found for an independently published identical table, but this does not change the special-case coverage finding.
